title: The Teletype and the Townhouse: Seattle, Albuquerque, Redmond, and the Long Reckoning
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Laurelhurst, the third William Henry Gates
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the city: Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates' gives the birth as 28 October 1955 in Seattle. The Laurelhurst placement is neighborhood-level only. No childhood street address was pinned in any source reached this pass, and the coordinate marks the Laurelhurst and Sand Point area rather than a house. The household detail comes from Wallace and Erickson, Hard Drive (1992), and the Smithsonian computer-history profile.
stops.campa: A son is born to William H. Gates II, a Seattle lawyer, and Mary Maxwell Gates, who sits on corporate and charitable boards across the city. They name him for his father and his grandfather, the third of that line, and call him Trey. He grows up with two sisters, Kristi and Libby, in a household that runs on competition: card games, board games, contests at the dinner table, all of them kept score of. The house stands in Laurelhurst, above Lake Washington, among lawyers and doctors and university families.
sources: Wallace and Erickson, Hard Drive: Bill Gates and the Making of the Microsoft Empire (1992)
suggested_refs: The Laurelhurst and Sand Point district of Seattle in the 1950s and 1960s

stops.name: Lakeside School, the Mothers' Club terminal
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month and day defaulted to 01; the sources give only that he entered Lakeside at about thirteen and first reached a computer there. Coordinates corrected: the research pool carried 47.7027 by -122.2846, which falls in the Lake Forest Park area some 4.5 km northeast of the campus. Wikipedia's 'Lakeside School (Seattle)' gives 47.73214 by -122.32753 for the 1st Avenue NE campus, used here.
stops.campa: At thirteen he is sent to Lakeside, a private school north of the city, where the Mothers' Club spends the takings of a rummage sale on a Teletype terminal wired to a computer somewhere else. Time on the machine costs money by the minute. He and Paul Allen and Kent Evans and Ric Weiland use all of it they can get and then find ways to get more, writing a tic-tac-toe program, then a payroll system, then whatever a paying adult will ask for. He is a teenager with several years of programming behind him at a time when almost no teenager has any.
suggested_refs: The Lakeside Mothers' Club rummage sale of 1968 and the Teletype Model 33 it bought

stops.name: The Cascade Range, Kent Evans does not come back
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to place, attested only in outline as to fact. The death of Kent Evans in a mountaineering accident before his high-school graduation is carried by the Smithsonian computer-history material, by Wallace and Erickson, and by Gates's own repeated retrospective accounts; the research pool flagged that no primary account of the accident was refetched this pass. The exact site is unknown and the coordinate is a regional placeholder in the Cascades, not a landmark. Month and day not established.
stops.campa: Kent Evans is the closest of the collaborators, the one he talks business with, the one who reads the trade press with him and plans companies neither of them is old enough to run. Evans goes climbing in the Washington mountains and does not come back. Gates is told at school. He is sixteen. Allen comes in to finish the class-scheduling program the two of them had been building, and the work gets done, and the friend stays dead. Gates has returned to it in interviews for fifty years without ever quite finishing the sentence.
sources: dossier lead, unconfirmed against a primary account
suggested_refs: Gates's own recorded recollections of Kent Evans, given repeatedly across five decades of interviews

stops.name: The United States Capitol, a page in the House
stops.date_confidence: the page service is attested by the Smithsonian computer-history profile, which gives the year 1972 and no month; the month here is a placeholder chosen only to order the segment before his final Lakeside year, and should not be read as a date. The Capitol coordinate is the building, which is where House pages worked, not a specific room.
stops.campa: He serves a stint as a page in the House of Representatives, carrying documents through the corridors of the Capitol in the summer the Watergate break-in happens a mile and a half away. The page corps takes boys of that age from all over the country for a season at a time, and he is one of them. He is sixteen, in a jacket, in a building full of men who will never hear of him. The account is brief in every telling: he goes, he works, he comes back to Seattle to finish school. What he made of it is not recorded anywhere reachable.
suggested_refs: The United States House of Representatives page program as it operated in the early 1970s

stops.name: Lakeside School, the score and the scheduler
stops.date_confidence: graduation year 1973 attested by Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates', which also carries the reported 1590 of 1600 college-board score; the month is the ordinary Lakeside commencement month and is not separately sourced. The story that he arranged his own class placement is his own, told in later interviews, and is carried here as his account rather than as an independent finding.
stops.campa: He graduates from Lakeside in the spring, having scored, by the account repeated ever since, 1590 out of 1600 on the college board examination. He is a National Merit Scholar. The class-scheduling program he and Evans began is running the school's timetable, and by his own later telling he has arranged his own placement into classes with a favourable ratio of girls. His father would prefer law. Harvard takes him, and he leaves for Cambridge in September.
suggested_refs: The Lakeside class-scheduling program, begun with Kent Evans and completed with Paul Allen

stops.name: Currier House, Cambridge, the room the deals came from
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates' gives the autumn 1973 matriculation, and Wikipedia's 'Currier House (Harvard College)' states that Gates and Ballmer met in Currier House, lived on the same floor, and that Gates made one of his first software deals from his room there. Coordinates corrected from the pool's 42.3838 by -71.1259, about 235 m off, to the Currier House figure 42.38169 by -71.12577 at 64 Linnaean Street. The pancake-sorting result was published later, in 1979.
stops.campa: He enters Harvard in the autumn and is housed in Currier House, in the Radcliffe Quadrangle, where a sophomore named Steve Ballmer lives on the same floor. He takes graduate mathematics and a combinatorics course and works on the pancake-sorting problem: given a stack of pancakes of different sizes and a spatula, how many flips are needed to put them in order. The bound he obtains with Christos Papadimitriou is published in 1979 and stands for three decades. He is also playing poker most nights and attending very few of his own lectures.
sources: Gates and Papadimitriou, 'Bounds for sorting by prefix reversal', Discrete Mathematics 27 (1979)
suggested_refs: Gates and Papadimitriou, 'Bounds for sorting by prefix reversal', Discrete Mathematics 27 (1979)

stops.name: MITS, Albuquerque, the tape that had never been run
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month and day defaulted to 01. The Smithsonian computer-history profile carries the demonstration, the PDP-10 simulator, and Monte Davidoff's part in writing the interpreter; the standard accounts place the flight and demonstration in the early months of 1975, but no primary source fixing the day was refetched in this pass. The MITS address on Linn Avenue NE is as given in the research pool and was not independently reverified.
stops.campa: Allen flies to New Mexico carrying a paper tape. The BASIC interpreter he and Gates and Monte Davidoff have written for the Altair 8800 has never been run on an Altair; they wrote it against a simulator on a Harvard PDP-10, working from the machine's specification sheet. Ed Roberts loads the tape at MITS. It prints READY. Nothing about the arrangement is legally tidy and the computer time was not theirs to spend, but the interpreter works on the first real machine it ever meets, and Gates takes a leave from Harvard that turns out to be permanent.
suggested_refs: The Altair 8800 and the MITS demonstration of Altair BASIC, Albuquerque, 1975

stops.name: Albuquerque, the open letter to the hobbyists
stops.date_confidence: attested and directly fetched: the full archival transcript of the letter, dated 3 February 1976 and circulated in the Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter, is hosted at digibarn.com and was read in full during research. All four quoted lines in this file's Albuquerque material are verbatim from that text. The office placement at Two Park Central Tower is a reconstruction, tagged [R] in the pool: the letter's own dateline gives Albuquerque, not a street.
stops.campa: Altair BASIC circulates faster than it sells. Paper tapes are copied at club meetings and passed hand to hand, and the royalty reaching Micro-Soft on each machine comes to almost nothing. Gates, twenty years old, writes an open letter to the Homebrew Computer Club and the hobby newsletters. It is reprinted, argued over, and answered furiously, and it fixes the terms of a quarrel about software and property that has not ended. The accusation is in the first line: who cares, he asks, if the people who worked on it get paid.
stops.quote: As the majority of hobbyists must be aware, most of you steal your software. Hardware must be paid for, but software is something to share. Who cares if the people who worked on it get paid?
stops.quote_source: William Henry Gates III, 'An Open Letter to Hobbyists', 3 February 1976, Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter; archival transcript at digibarn.com
sources: digibarn.com archival transcript of 'An Open Letter to Hobbyists', fetched in full
suggested_refs: 'An Open Letter to Hobbyists', 3 February 1976, in the Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter

stops.name: Two Park Central Tower, the name registered
stops.date_confidence: the registration date, 26 November 1976, is attested by Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates'. The Two Park Central Tower office is tagged [R] in the research pool: Albuquerque is certain, the specific building is the commonly reported address and was not independently reverified. The founding of Micro-Soft itself is dated only to 1975 in the sources reached, which is why this stop carries the registration rather than the founding.
stops.campa: The company works out of rented offices in a tower on University Boulevard, a dozen young men and the occasional mattress on the floor, writing language interpreters for every microprocessor that appears. Nobody in the industry yet believes a licence is worth much on its own. Gates handles the contracts himself and keeps the terms narrow anyway: the customer buys the right to ship the software, never the software. On the twenty-sixth of November the trade name Microsoft is registered with the Secretary of State of New Mexico, the hyphen gone.
suggested_refs: The New Mexico trade-name registration of 26 November 1976

stops.name: Bernalillo County, the photograph against the height chart
stops.date_confidence: year only; month and day defaulted to 01. The Smithsonian computer-history profile carries a 1977 Albuquerque traffic matter and the resulting booking photograph. The specific charge, the court, and the disposition were not established from any primary record reached this pass, and the coordinate is central Albuquerque rather than a verified courthouse or jail address.
stops.campa: He is stopped in Albuquerque over a traffic matter and photographed against the height chart: hair to his collar, a half smile, twenty-one years old. He has a local reputation for driving fast. The offence is minor and the surviving record of it is thin. The photograph is not thin. It is reproduced for the next half century on posters and mugs and magazine covers, in every profile that needs an image of the boy before the fortune, and it has long outlived any account of what he was actually charged with.
suggested_refs: The 1977 Albuquerque booking photograph of William H. Gates III

stops.name: Bellevue, the company comes home
stops.date_confidence: attested: Microsoft's own corporate history gives 1 January 1979 for the relocation from Albuquerque to Bellevue, Washington. The Old National Bank Building on NE 8th Street is the address carried in the research pool for the first Bellevue offices; the coordinate was not independently reverified this pass. Employee and revenue figures for 1979 are given in round terms because no audited primary figure was fetched.
stops.campa: On the first day of the year Microsoft moves out of New Mexico and into offices in Bellevue, across Lake Washington from the city he grew up in. There are about a dozen employees. The company sells programming languages to hardware makers who have no software of their own, and its revenue for the year runs to a few million dollars. Gates is twenty-three, president, and the person who reads every contract before it is signed. His mother's board seats and his father's law practice are ten minutes away.
suggested_refs: The Old National Bank Building at 10800 NE 8th Street, Bellevue, Microsoft's first Washington address

stops.name: Boca Raton, the secret division
stops.date_confidence: year given as a placeholder to order the segment; the negotiations ran across 1980 and 1981 and no single day is fixed in the sources reached. Microsoft's own corporate history and the Smithsonian profile both carry the Boca Raton Entry Systems Division, the failed Digital Research talks over CP/M, and the return to Microsoft. The terms of the resulting contract are described here in the form in which they are universally reported; the contract itself was not read in this pass.
stops.campa: IBM builds its personal computer in Florida, away from its own bureaucracy, on a schedule of about a year. The team needs an operating system. Talks with Digital Research over CP/M come to nothing, and the team comes back to Microsoft, which has no operating system either. Gates says yes anyway. Nobody else in 1980 is building this machine, so the clause IBM concedes costs IBM nothing: Microsoft may license to anyone it likes the same system it is licensing to IBM.
suggested_refs: The IBM Entry Systems Division at Boca Raton and the Project Chess development schedule

stops.name: Tukwila, the system they bought
stops.date_confidence: the licence and the 1981 outright purchase of 86-DOS from Seattle Computer Products are attested by Microsoft's own facts page; the exact date of the purchase was not fixed in this pass and the month and day are defaulted. The IBM PC announcement of 12 August 1981 is a dossier lead corroborated by standard histories but not refetched from a primary IBM announcement. The Washington reincorporation of 25 June 1981 is attested by Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates'. Seattle Computer Products' exact address at the time of sale is not confirmed; Tukwila is the commonly reported location.
stops.campa: The operating system Microsoft has promised IBM is written by Tim Paterson at Seattle Computer Products, twenty minutes south of Bellevue, and is called QDOS, for quick and dirty. Microsoft licenses it, then in 1981 buys it outright, adapts it, and ships it to IBM as PC DOS. The IBM PC is announced on the twelfth of August. In June the company has reincorporated in Washington State with Gates as president and chairman. Seattle Computer Products later sues over what it was and was not told at the time of the sale.
sources: dossier lead for the 12 August 1981 IBM PC announcement
suggested_refs: Tim Paterson's 86-DOS, written at Seattle Computer Products and sold to Microsoft in 1981

stops.name: Redmond, the first retail Windows
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates' for the 20 November 1985 retail release. The account of tiled rather than overlapping windows and of the product's poor early reception is standard industry history and is not carried by a primary source fetched in this pass. The graphical lineage running through Xerox PARC is well documented but no personal visit by Gates to PARC is attested in anything reached, which is why this file carries no PARC stop.
stops.campa: Two years late, and after a public demonstration that preceded any working code, the first retail version of Windows ships on the twentieth of November: a graphical shell laid over DOS, its windows tiled rather than overlapping, because overlapping windows are a matter of litigation. Reviewers find it slow and short of programs to run. Who invented the interface is by then a question for the courts. Gates does not stop shipping it. Versions follow in 1987 and 1990 and 1992 before anything about the product is widely admired.
sources: United States District Court, Findings of Fact, United States v. Microsoft Corp.
suggested_refs: The graphical-interface research demonstrated at Xerox PARC, Palo Alto, and its passage into both the Macintosh and Windows

stops.name: Redmond, twenty-one dollars a share
stops.date_confidence: attested: Microsoft's own account of the flotation gives 13 March 1986, the twenty-one dollar offer price, Gates's sale of about 1.6 million dollars of stock, and his retained holding of roughly 45 percent then valued near 350 million. The February 1986 move to the Redmond campus is from the same source. The 1987 Forbes youngest-self-made-billionaire count is attested by Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates'.
stops.campa: Microsoft moves onto a new campus in Redmond in February and goes public in March at twenty-one dollars a share. Gates sells about one and a half million dollars of stock and keeps roughly forty-five percent of the company, worth some three hundred and fifty million on the day. The next year Forbes counts him, at thirty-one, the youngest self-made billionaire it has recorded. The campus keeps growing outward around him, building by building, and he goes on working out of one of them for another twenty years.
suggested_refs: The Microsoft initial public offering of 13 March 1986

stops.name: The Prettyman Courthouse, the suit and the tape
stops.date_confidence: the filing date, 18 May 1998, and the twenty state attorneys general are attested by Wikipedia's 'United States v. Microsoft Corp.'. Coordinates corrected from the pool's 38.8951 by -77.0164, about 230 m off, to Wikipedia's figure for the E. Barrett Prettyman courthouse at 333 Constitution Avenue NW. The deposition is placed here because this is the courtroom in which the tape entered the record and was played; where and on exactly which days it was recorded is not established in any source reached, and this stop should not be read as fixing the recording's location.
stops.campa: The Department of Justice and twenty state attorneys general file suit on the eighteenth of May, alleging that Microsoft has abused a monopoly in personal-computer operating systems, chiefly by binding its browser into Windows against Netscape, the company Marc Andreessen co-founded. Gates is deposed on videotape. Extracts run on the evening news. Played into this courtroom, the tape shows him rocking in his chair, quarrelling with the meaning of ordinary words, saying he does not recall.
sources: marc_andreessen.journey.json, stop of 21 June 1995 at Netscape headquarters
suggested_refs: The Gates deposition tapes of 1998, as played into the record in United States v. Microsoft Corp.

stops.name: Washington, the findings of fact
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia's 'United States v. Microsoft Corp.' gives 5 November 1999 for Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson's findings that Microsoft's dominance of the x86 personal-computer operating-system market constituted a monopoly. The share-price movement and the company's public response are general contemporaneous reporting and were not refetched from a primary source this pass.
stops.campa: Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson issues his findings of fact on the fifth of November. Microsoft holds monopoly power in the market for x86 personal-computer operating systems; it has used that power against rivals, against competing technologies, and to the harm of consumers. The findings are not the judgment, only the court's account of what happened, and they are written to survive appeal. The share price falls. Gates, chairman and chief executive of a company a federal court has just called a monopolist, issues a statement disagreeing with all of it.
suggested_refs: Findings of Fact, United States v. Microsoft Corp., 5 November 1999

stops.name: Redmond, giving up the title
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day defaulted to 01: Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates' gives January 2000 for the handover of the chief executive's role to Steve Ballmer and Gates's assumption of the title chief software architect, with the chairmanship retained. The reading of the move as a response to the antitrust trial is contemporaneous commentary, not a finding, and is marked as such in the campa.
stops.campa: In January he hands the chief executive's office to Steve Ballmer, whom he met on the fourth floor of Currier House in 1973, and takes for himself the title of chief software architect. He stays chairman. Outside the company the move is read as a response to the trial; inside it, as what Gates has wanted for years, which is the code rather than the org chart. Ballmer runs Microsoft for the next fourteen years. Gates keeps an office, keeps the largest single block of stock, and starts giving his afternoons to the foundation.
suggested_refs: The January 2000 Microsoft succession announcement

stops.name: Washington, the order to break it in two
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia's 'United States v. Microsoft Corp.' gives 7 June 2000 for Jackson's order that Microsoft be broken into two separate companies. That the order never took effect follows from the appellate reversal of 28 June 2001, attested in the same article.
stops.campa: Jackson orders Microsoft split into two companies, one holding the operating system and one holding everything else. It is the remedy the government asked for and the outcome the industry has argued about for two years. Gates has spent a decade saying in public that the case was about nothing, and he gives no ground now. Microsoft appeals the same day. Through the whole of the interval the company operates exactly as it has always operated, and the order never takes effect.
suggested_refs: Jackson's remedies order of 7 June 2000 and the immediate Microsoft appeal

stops.name: Washington, overturned and then settled
stops.date_confidence: both events attested by Wikipedia's 'United States v. Microsoft Corp.': the D.C. Circuit overturned the breakup on 28 June 2001 while leaving the findings on monopolistic conduct standing, and Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly approved the settlement on 1 November 2002. This stop is dated to the settlement and carries the appellate reversal in its campa; the appellate court's criticism of Jackson's contacts with the press is standard reporting of the opinion and was not read from the opinion itself in this pass.
stops.campa: The Court of Appeals throws out the breakup in June 2001, in part because Jackson had discussed the case with reporters while presiding over it, and lets the findings on monopolistic conduct stand. What follows is a settlement rather than a dismemberment. In November 2002 Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly approves terms requiring Microsoft to share programming interfaces with third parties and to submit to a technical committee for five years. The company is not broken up and no line of its code is changed by the judgment. The findings of fact stay on the record.
suggested_refs: United States v. Microsoft Corp., 253 F.3d 34 (D.C. Cir. 2001), and the final judgment of 1 November 2002

segments.name: The House, the Mother, and the Foundation

stops.name: Manele Bay, Lanai, the wedding
stops.date_confidence: attested for date and island: Wikipedia's 'Bill Gates' gives the marriage to Melinda French on 1 January 1994 on Lanai. Corrected from the research pool on one point: Wikipedia's 'Melinda French Gates' says she joined Microsoft in 1987 as a multimedia product developer, not as a product manager. Manele Bay coordinates are within tolerance of the bay itself; no venue address was verified.
stops.campa: He marries Melinda Ann French on the first of January on Lanai, the small Hawaiian island, in a wedding closed tightly enough that no photographer can shoot it from the golf course. She joined Microsoft in 1987 as a multimedia product developer and has risen to general manager. They met there seven years ago. He is thirty-eight. His mother Mary, who has five months to live, has pressed him for years to say what he intends the money to be for, and she is at the wedding.
suggested_refs: Contemporary coverage of the January 1994 wedding on Lanai

stops.name: Laurelhurst, his mother's house
stops.date_confidence: attested and corrected upward from the research pool's [R] tag: Wikipedia's 'Mary Maxwell Gates' states that she died at age 64 on 10 June 1994 at her home in the Laurelhurst neighborhood of Seattle after suffering from breast cancer for several months. Date, cause, and place are all confirmed there, as is her full name, Mary Ann Gates, born Maxwell. Her United Way and University of Washington roles are from the same article. The coordinate is the neighborhood, not the house.
stops.campa: Mary Ann Gates, born Maxwell, dies of breast cancer at her home in Laurelhurst on the tenth of June, sixty-four years old, five months after her son's wedding. She had been a regent of the University of Washington and the first woman to chair the national board of United Way, and it was on boards like those, not in the software business, that she learned how to ask people with money what they intended to do with it. The foundation that will carry the family name is six years away. She had put that question to her son directly and more than once.
suggested_refs: Mary Maxwell Gates's tenure on the national board of United Way of America

stops.name: Medina, the house on the lake
stops.date_confidence: the house and its scale are attested: Wikipedia's article on the residence confirms the 66,000 square feet and gives 47.62774 by -122.24194, which corrects the research pool's -122.2312, a figure that put the estate roughly 830 m east of the parcel and out over the water. The completion year is reported variously across accounts and the 1997 date here is an ordering placeholder rather than a verified completion date. The 2007 wealth-ranking claim is carried from carlos_slim.journey.json, whose own stop records private calculations that year ranking Slim first, ahead of Gates.
stops.campa: The house on the Medina shore of Lake Washington is finished after years of building: some sixty-six thousand square feet dug into the hillside, earth-sheltered, wired so that a guest wears a pin telling the walls which pictures to show and what temperature to hold. The press calls it Xanadu 2.0. Forbes has had him at the head of its list of the world's richest people since 1995; in 2007 private calculations circulate putting Carlos Slim, in Mexico City, ahead of him. He lives in this house for the next quarter century.
suggested_refs: The Medina estate on Lake Washington, popularly called Xanadu 2.0

stops.name: Seattle, Fifth Avenue North, the foundation
stops.date_confidence: the foundation's 2000 formation and its Seattle base are attested by its own fact sheet. Coordinates corrected from the pool's -122.3572, about 870 m west toward Elliott Avenue, to Wikipedia's figure for the Gates Foundation campus, 47.62361 by -122.34556. The spend-down commitment, more than 200 billion dollars and closure on 31 December 2045, is attested by the May 2025 announcement on gatesnotes.com and the foundation's own fact sheet. Buffett's giving is attested; his later ending of the partnership belongs to 2026 and is carried on a later stop.
stops.campa: The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation is formed from two earlier trusts and takes an endowment larger than any private foundation has ever held. Its work is vaccines, malaria, tuberculosis, polio, sanitation, seed varieties, and American schools. Its money pays for results that governments will not fund, and it buys, with nobody voting on it, the power to set the agenda of global health. Warren Buffett gives it the greater part of his own fortune. Its declared plan is to spend more than two hundred billion dollars and close on the last day of 2045.
suggested_refs: The Gates Foundation fact sheet and the May 2025 spend-down announcement

stops.name: Cambridge, the degree he came back for
stops.date_confidence: the honorary Doctor of Laws and the Commencement address are attested by Harvard's commencement records and the Smithsonian profile; June 2007 is firm, and the day here follows Harvard's commencement date for that year but was not independently reverified. The coordinate is the Harvard Yard and Cambridge area rather than Currier House, since the ceremony was held in the Yard. The quoted lines are given as reported summary, not as a verbatim transcript, and no quote field is set for that reason.
stops.campa: Thirty-two years after leaving without one, Harvard gives him an honorary doctorate of laws and the Commencement address. He opens by telling his father that he always said he would come back and get his degree. Then he tells the graduating class that he left this university knowing very little about the inequities of the world, that nobody taught him about the millions of children dying of diseases that could be prevented, and that this was the great regret of his education. He is fifty-one years old.
suggested_refs: Bill Gates, Harvard Commencement address, June 2007

stops.name: Redmond, the last full-time day
stops.date_confidence: the date is widely reported and was tagged [R] in the research pool because no primary Microsoft announcement was refetched this pass. The chairmanship was retained until 2014 and that is separately attested. The send-off described in the campa is standard contemporaneous reporting of the day and is not carried by a primary source read here.
stops.campa: On the twenty-seventh of June he works his last day as a full-time employee of the company he founded thirty-three years earlier. He is fifty-two, and has spent the whole of his adult life at one company. He keeps the chairmanship and an office on the campus. From here the foundation takes most of his week. The handover has been announced two years in advance and rehearsed in public through both of them, and the day itself is marked with a video and jokes about his calendar.
sources: dossier lead, widely reported, not refetched from a primary Microsoft announcement
suggested_refs: The two-year Microsoft transition plan announced in June 2006

stops.name: San Diego, the harsh mathematics of polio
stops.date_confidence: attested and corrected: the research pool first carried this quotation as a foundation speech of 12 December 2009 sourced to Wikiquote. The primary source is the prepared remarks to the Rotary International Assembly, San Diego, 21 January 2009, published on gatesfoundation.org, and the verbatim text differs from the Wikiquote rendering in three places. The coordinate is central San Diego; the assembly venue was not established, and the coordinate should be read as the city, not the hall.
stops.campa: He stands in front of the Rotary International Assembly, the service organization that has been raising money to end polio since 1985, and makes the case in arithmetic rather than in compassion. Rotarians have funded this campaign for a generation and the foundation matches what they raise. The eradication effort is three decades old at this point and it is not finished. Polio cannot be held at a low level: a thousand cases a year is not a floor, it is a launching point, and the number climbs again the moment anyone stops paying.
stops.quote: The harsh mathematics of polio makes it clear: We cannot maintain a level of 1,000 or 2,000 cases a year. Either we eradicate polio or we return to the days of tens of thousands of cases per year.
stops.quote_source: Bill Gates, prepared remarks to the Rotary International Assembly, San Diego, 21 January 2009, gatesfoundation.org
suggested_refs: Rotary International's PolioPlus campaign, begun 1985, and its matching arrangement with the Gates Foundation

stops.name: Khammam district, the demonstration project
stops.date_confidence: the project ran across 2009 and 2010; the year here is an ordering placeholder and the month and day are defaulted to 01. The vaccination of roughly 23,000 girls across Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, the reported deaths, the Indian parliamentary committee's criticism of consent and oversight, and the failure of later review to establish causation are all attested by Science's account of the parliamentary report. Khammam district is one of the project sites and the coordinate is the district, not a clinic.
stops.campa: A demonstration project funded by the foundation and run by PATH vaccinates roughly twenty-three thousand girls against human papillomavirus across Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat. Deaths are reported among the participants. An Indian parliamentary committee investigates and condemns the consent procedures and the oversight, finding girls enrolled through schools and hostels without informed consent from anyone entitled to give it. The report is still cited against the foundation fifteen years on. The project is halted. Later review does not establish that the vaccine caused the deaths.
suggested_refs: The 72nd report of the Indian Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, on the HPV demonstration project

stops.name: Bellevue, a company for a different reactor
stops.date_confidence: attested and corrected upward from the pool's [R] tag: Wikipedia's 'TerraPower' gives the 2006 founding by Bill Gates and the Bellevue, Washington headquarters. Month and day are defaulted to 01. The coordinate reuses this file's Bellevue pin, the Old National Bank Building, because no separate TerraPower street address was verified; it should be read as Bellevue, not as the company's door.
stops.campa: He founds a nuclear company in Bellevue, a few miles from where Microsoft first landed after New Mexico. TerraPower's premise is that the reactor design the world settled on in the 1960s was not the only one available, and that a sodium-cooled fast reactor with a molten-salt heat store can be built to follow a grid full of wind and sun.
